rationale: C02, issued only nine days earlier by the same President, plausibly supplied concrete language and structure for the child proclamation. Both invoke section 2 of the 1906 act, reserve federal land as part of a national monument subject to existing rights, follow the operative reservation with a detailed land description, and use an unusually close warning clause including the sequence “appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove” and the prohibition on locating or settling upon lands reserved by the proclamation. C17 and C23 share much of this machinery, but C02 is the closest in timing and literal formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: by virtue of the authority vested In me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 225 (16 U.S.C. 431), do proclaim that, subject to valid existing rights, there is hereby reserved and set apart as a national monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906, 34 Stat. 225 (16 U.S.C. 431), do proclaim that the following-described lands are hereby added to and reserved as a part of the Bandelier National Monument
shared_material.explanation: The same statutory invocation leads directly into materially parallel monument-reservation language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Warning is hereby given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of this monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved by this proclamation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Warning is hereby expressly given to all unauthorized persons not to appropriate, injure, destroy, deface, or remove any feature of the area herein added to the monument and not to locate or settle upon any of the lands reserved by this proclamation.
shared_material.explanation: This is a near-verbatim, distinctive warning provision with the same five prohibited acts and identical concluding restriction.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Chesapeake and Ohio Canal National Monument shall be supervised, managed, and controlled in accordance with the act of Congress entitled “An Act To Establish a National Park Service and for Other Purposes,” approved August 25, 1916
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The lands described above shall be subject to all laws and regulations applicable to the Bandelier National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both place the newly reserved lands into the established legal and administrative regime governing national monuments, although the child states that machinery more explicitly.
